picks.headline: Apollo: an AI model that fills the gaps in damaged ancient Greek papyri
picks.excerpt: Researchers developed Apollo, a large language model that fills in the gaps in damaged ancient Greek papyrus fragments to help read and translate tattered historical texts.
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool and the only new release: a purpose-built LLM for restoring and reading lost texts, a concrete case of AI extending what can be read at all rather than another policy fight.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: keep it on the reading/translation of texts (restoring damaged papyri, what scholars can now read) — not a generic 'AI model' story. CROSS-SECTION RISK: this WIRED piece could also be picked by the science section today; the orchestrator should check selected_science.json and keep it in only one section (card id + pipeline/media/ file collide otherwise).

picks.headline: Disclosing AI Use in Academic Research: A New Global Study from Oxford University Press
picks.excerpt: Oxford University Press updated author and editor guidelines with a policy on what AI use must be disclosed in manuscripts, alongside a survey of 2,600+ researchers on AI disclosure.
picks.rationale: The most actionable item in the pool: a major press's new AI-disclosure rule for manuscripts, with data from a survey of 2,600+ researchers. Authors submitting to OUP have to comply with it now.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: lead with what OUP now requires authors to disclose, then the survey numbers. Oldest item in the five (09-10); frame it as the policy now in force, not as breaking news.

picks.headline: Damned If You Do, Damned If You Don't: Multilingual Researchers' Use of AI in Academic Writing
picks.excerpt: Generative AI has made language tools ubiquitous for multilingual researchers, but it introduces risks of homogenized texts and semantic slippage — and suspicion from journals either way.
picks.rationale: Pairs with the OUP disclosure rule from the writer's side: non-native-English authors are suspected whether they use AI or not, which is the equity cost of the disclosure regimes journals are adopting.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: the 2026-09-17 card books-llm-homogenises-writing (The Bookseller) covered homogenisation in general. Lead here on the multilingual researcher's double bind with journals, and give homogenisation one clause at most.

picks.headline: Feeling overwhelmed by the AI doom loop? Here's the essential reading list to make sense of it all
picks.excerpt: Guardian reporters and experts recommend the books that explain how the AI industry got here and where it is headed, amid a chaotic moment reshaping our lives.
picks.rationale: AI is the whole subject (45 mentions): a curated list of books about the AI industry. It is the only reader-facing item in the pool and a new outlet for the section, which balances the three scholarly-publishing picks.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: name specific titles and authors from the list and say what each helps a reader understand. Do not write a generic 'AI anxiety' piece.

picks.headline: Just Released: Clarivate Releases Pulse of the Library 2026
picks.excerpt: Clarivate's Pulse of the Library 2026 finds a widening gap between libraries actively implementing AI and those still experimenting; 16% globally report moderate-to-active AI implementation.
picks.rationale: AI adoption is the report's main finding, and it comes with hard numbers (16% of libraries worldwide at moderate-to-active AI implementation, and a widening gap). It is data, not opinion, so it beats the SK Groupthink essay for the last slot. infoDOCKET reaches its 2-card outlet cap here.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: lead with the numbers on the gap between libraries that are implementing AI and those still experimenting. The survey is vendor-published, so attribute findings to Clarivate. Keep it distinct from books-ital-genai-libraries (09-22) and books-crl-digitization (09-20): this card is about adoption rates, not integration case studies or digitization terms. This is the oldest item (09-09), so frame it as the current state of play.
